title: Mock exam 1: a full 65-question baseline

kcs.statement: A mock predicts the real exam only when taken in one sitting, closed-book and timed at 90 minutes for 65 questions with every question answered; pausing, looking up answers or reusing seen questions inflates the score.

A domain score is the number of correct answers in that domain divided by that domain's question count, and it is recorded for each of the four domains because a strong overall percentage can hide one domain below 70%.

problem_ideas: Take mock 1 (65 questions, 90 minutes) and fill in the score sheet: overall percentage plus four domain scores.
You got 11 of 15 Domain 2 items right; compute the domain score and say whether it clears 70%.
Your overall is 81% but Domain 4 is 3 of 6; decide whether mock 1 meets the course bar.
A learner paused the mock for lunch and checked two answers online; estimate how that biases the score and what to do.
Compare your minute-60 checkpoint with the pacing plan and note how many items were flagged.
From a list of 65 answered items tagged by domain, compute all four domain scores in under five minutes.
Predict your Domain 3 score before seeing results, then compare with the actual score to calibrate.
